purpose: Track candidate real APKs for the APK-to-SBOM research dataset before they are admitted into source-validated, smoke, or limitation layers.
admission_rule: APK file and SHA-256 are stored.
Exact source tag or commit is recorded.
APK versionName/versionCode is compared with source metadata.
Resolved Gradle dependency tree is stored.
Source validation report is generated when source validation is claimed.
Dataset classification row is present in the inventory.

priority_statuses.admitted: Already in the dataset with proof artifacts.
priority_statuses.M1-candidate: First milestone candidate; validate these before scaling.
priority_statuses.M2-candidate: Good expansion candidate after the first 5-20 real APKs work.
priority_statuses.limitation-candidate: Chosen mainly to test a known boundary such as native-heavy, packed, Flutter, Unity, or dynamic-code behavior.

candidates.reason: Tests a React Native/native-heavy framework boundary where Java/Kotlin DEX SBOM evidence is incomplete and source dependency-tree validation needs a larger Node/npm toolchain.
proof_notes: APK manifest package/version matches F-Droid target `org.jitsi.meet` versionCode `26000004` and versionName `26.0.0`.
F-Droid metadata for versionCode `26000004` points to source commit `3db92da369b921d73189dbcb55744f9f5459cac0`, subdir `android/app`, and React Native prebuild steps.
The calibrated report `data/results/report-real-jitsi-meet/` emits 7 candidate-confidence Maven SBOM components, 13 native file components, and one potential Gson advisory; no advisory is confirmed.

Gradle `9.5.0` is incompatible with this source build because it imports `org.gradle.util.VersionNumber`; Gradle `8.14` reaches React Native configuration but fails because `node` is missing in the Docker runtime.
F-Droid also requires cmake, emscripten, esbuild, make, NDK 27.1/26.1, matrix-olm, and `npm install --build-from-source`; keep Jitsi out of accuracy metrics until the resolved dependency tree exists.
